name: Task list
summary: Use a task list to show the tasks in a multi-part service and help users understand which are complete or still need attention.
whenToUse: Use for services with several tasks that users may complete over time or in a flexible order.
Show a clear current status for each task and link only tasks the user can open.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for a short linear journey where normal page navigation is clearer.
Do not use as a generic navigation menu or checklist unrelated to completing a service.

anatomy.name: Task list
anatomy.description: A govuk-task-list ul contains one li per task.

anatomy.name: Task name and hint
anatomy.description: The task has a concise name, optional hint and an href only when it is available.

anatomy.name: Status
anatomy.description: A uniquely identified status is referenced from the task link using aria-describedby.

variants.name: Linked task
variants.use: A task the user can currently open.

variants.name: Unlinked task
variants.use: A task that is unavailable or does not have a destination.

behaviour: No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required; links navigate to the corresponding task.
Derive status from authoritative service data and update it after task completion.
Do not make the status itself the only clickable target when the task name is the destination.
accessibility: Associate each link with its unique status ID using aria-describedby.
Status text must be meaningful without its tag colour.
Keep list order and task availability understandable to keyboard and screen-reader users.
content: Name each task with a concise verb phrase or recognisable subject.
Use a small consistent status vocabulary, such as “Not started”, “In progress” and “Completed”.
Add hint text only when the task name does not provide enough context.
